title.narrative: GEM Report Contribution agreement

description.narrative: Contribution agreement to finance the implementation of the action Global Education Monitoring Report. The GEM Report is an editorially independent, authoritative, and evidence-based annual report that monitors progress on education in the SDGs. Its mandate is to be the mechanism for monitoring and reporting on SDG 4 and on education in the other SDGs and on the implementation of national and international strategies to help hold all relevant partners to account for their commitments.''

description.narrative: Number of global, national or local development policies or programmes influenced by the GEM Report.

comment.narrative: 5 examples of policy impact at global regional and national levelsGlobal The work of the GEM Report with the UIS on the national SDG 4 benchmarks apart from helping fulfil one of the neglected commitments of the Education 2030 Framework for Action has a range of farreaching implications aligning national regional and global targets in education ensuring national SDG 4 targets are not supplanted by externally set targets developing capacity in indicator use drawing attention to data gaps and spurring interest for initiatives that aim to fill them and drawing attention to the lack of targets in national sector plans. In February the 53rd session of the United Nations Statistical Commission supported the work undertaken by the UIS and the GEM Report team in setting regional and national benchmarks for selected SDG 4 indicators supported the update and revision mechanisms proposed for keeping the benchmarks relevant and appreciated the potential of the benchmarking approach in identifying data gaps in encouraging Member States to collect relevant education statistics and in promoting interregional and intraregional statistical cooperation in education.The Technical Cooperation Group approved the concept of estimating outofschool rates using a GEM Report and UISproposed method that combines administrative and survey data to make effective and efficient use of information enabling the generation of longterm data series due be released through the VIEW website in September.Regional The South Asia Association for Regional Cooperation agreed to host a launch event of the 2022 regional report on nonstate actors in South Asia which for the first time puts the issue to the attention of regional dialogue in education.A partnership agreement was negotiated between the GEM Report and the Southeast Asia Ministers of Education Organization for the preparation of a regional edition of the 2023 GEM Report on technology and education that will focus on the region which will enable the placement of the issue on the regional agenda.National The 2020 GEM Report recommendations were used as the basis for the recommendations made at the February 2022 Global Disability Summit where a total of 230 associated commitments were made in relation to inclusive education including for example by Rwanda which committed to train all Sector and District Level education offices by end 2024 in inclusive education and Malawi which committed to adopt a zerorejection policy at all levels of education in line with provisions of the Disability Act the Malawi Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities by 2022.The 20212 GEM Report shone a light on the cost of education pricing the poor out of a good quality education and specifically that 30 of families in Uganda must borrow to afford their childrens education. One month later the Report supported the case filed in the High Court of Uganda against the state for breach of its duty to protect respect and fulfil the right to education for all. In this civil suit the case called for better regulation of tuition and nontuition charges payable at any school or education institution in the country. The High Court subsequently tasked the Government to ensure equity in the design and implementation of education programmes it ordered that the Ministry of Education and Sports take a lead position in regulating private involvement in education to ensure compliance and adherence to minimum standards. The International Monetary Fund conducted a review of Article IV in South Africa and referenced the 2021 Education Finance Watch as one of its 14 sources for information. It recommended that ambitious fiscal consolidation is needed to reduce public debt while protecting the most vulnerable and that the budget should include better targeting of education subsidies.

title.narrative: Policy papers produced and launched.

description.narrative: Policy papers produced and launched.

comment.narrative: Policy Paper 47 entitled Nonstate actors in tertiary education a shared vision for quality and affordability was released in May 2022 at the World Higher Education Conference during a session coorganized with the International Network of Educational Institutions on equity and inclusion in higher education. The session featured academics University of Toronto University College London and University of WisconsinMadison regional organizations European Commission education leaders Universities South Africa nonstate actors private university in Colombia and students European Students Union. The paper draws upon the corresponding chapter in the global report on tertiary education. Policy Paper 48 entitled Outofschool numbers are growing in subSaharan Africa was released in September 2022. It is estimated that 244 million children and youth between the ages of 6 and 18 worldwide were out of school in 2021 of which 118.5 million were girls and 125.5 million were boys. The results are based on a new improved way of measuring outofschool rates by the GEM Report and the UIS displayed on the VIEW website. It combines administrative and survey data following a similar approach to the one applied before in the estimation of flagship health indicators. The estimates confirm that even before the onset of COVID19 progress in reducing the outofschool population had slowed down. At the same time the results suggest a different distribution of this population by age group while they fill gaps in the case of about 50 countries whose administrative data have been incomplete or lacking.The 2022 Education Finance Watch the second in a series launched in 2021 was released in June for the first day of the Transforming Education preSummit in partnership with the World Bank joined for the first time by the UIS. The series aims to provide an annual analysis of trends patterns and issues in education financing around the world. The report focused on the extent to which the COVID19 pandemic has affected education finance with substantially more data extending to 2022 budgets. It was produced along with a threepage summary three animations and a press release. It will be translated to all UN languages and will be accompanied by technical background information and the underlying datasets.The SDG 4 Data Digest UIS annual flagship publication was copublished with the GEM Report and released for International Day of Education in January. It focused on the steps taken to set national SDG 4 benchmarks up to the end of 2021 by which time almost 6 in 10 countries had set national targets for at least some of the 7 benchmark indicators. The report contains quotes from 15 countries about their experiences participating in the process as well as endorsements from Gordon Brown UN Special Envoy for Global Education David Edwards General Secretary of Education International Abdulla Shahid President of the United Nations General Assembly Jakaya Kikwete Chair of the GPE Board and Refat Sabbah President of the Global Campaign for Education. It has been downloaded 2500 times. Another publication Setting commitments provided updates on the benchmarking process was prepared with the UIS to feed into the SDG 4 review at the 2022 Highlevel Political Forum and the Transforming Education Summit convened by the UN SecretaryGeneral. This publication continues the GEM Report and UIS contribution at the 2019 Highlevel Political Forum Meeting Commitments and Beyond Commitments. It provides a summary of the process and its significance a proposal on how to regularly monitor benchmarks updates on the submitted benchmark values and their implications for achieving SDG 4 and a representative set of 12 country case studies describing their benchmarksetting processes and their link to national policies. It was published in English in July and in the other UN languages in September.

comment.narrative: 2 Gender and 1 youth reports produced and launchedGender ReportThe 2022 Gender Report was released in April 2022. As in previous editions it has a monitoring and a thematic part. The monitoring part covers gender gaps in learning outcomes in more depth. The thematic part focuses on nonstate actors. Three background papers were commissioned on private childcare private singlesex universities and private faithbased schools in Asia. The Report was launched along with a social media campaign Deepenthedebate and has since been downloaded over 5500 times. A video produced containing the main messages of the Report was viewed over 3000 times. The Report is being translated into French and Spanish.G7 Global Objectives on girls education report A new partnership with the United Kingdom Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office the United Nations Girls Education Initiative and the UIS focuses on a baseline report to support the monitoring of the two G7 global objectives on girls education set during the UK presidency in 2021 to be achieved by 2026 in low and lowermiddleincome countries 40 million more girls in school and 20 million achieving minimum proficiency in reading by the end of primary school. The report reviews the starting points and the prospects for achieving the two objectives discusses the experience of one country India showcases G7 flagship programmes based on a questionnaire shared with G7 member states and informs the G7 education and development agenda including the work of the accountability working group. The report was launched in October.Youth Report The 2022 Youth Report was launched in May at an inperson event along with a campaign to RighttheRules to make sure that the poorest are not priced out of a quality education. The report provides a youth perspective on the messages and recommendations of the 20212 GEM Report. It was produced in partnership with the Global Student Forum compiling views and voices of young people from a global consultation. It was released at the Board Meeting of the European Students Union with representatives from 45 youth organizations from over 40 countries marking the start of a regional series of events jointly organized with the All Africa Student Union the Commonwealth Students Association the Organizing Bureau of European Secondary Students the Organizacin Continental Latinoamericana y Caribea de Estudiantes and with associations in Canada and New Zealand. It has been downloaded 1100 times since launch. It is being translated into French and Spanish.

comment.narrative: 2 Regional reports published and launchedSpotlight Report on universal primary education completion and foundational learning in AfricaThe Spotlight series a partnership with the Association for the Development of Education in Africa ADEA aims to elevate these completion and learning in the list of continental priorities through research and analysis peer learning and accountability mechanisms and advocacy and outreach activities. The work leverages the GEM Report teams strengths in research analysis and advocacy as well as ADEAs leading role in education policy dialogue and country level reach.The first continental report Born to Learn synthesizes evidence on completion rates and levels of minimum learning proficiency in the continent informing the debate on national SDG 4 CESA benchmarks. It draws on five country reports covering the Democratic Republic of the Congo Ghana Mozambique Rwanda and Senegal and a series of case studies from all African regions which were all launched at ADEAs Triennale in Mauritius on 20 October 2022.South Asia Report on nonstate actors in educationThe 2022 Regional Report on nonstate actors in education focuses on South Asia and its release is scheduled for November 2022. The completed draft builds on the 20212 GEM Report conceptualization with further inhouse research and substantial primary data collection as well as continuous engagements with external authors and partners. Eight country studies have been developed on Afghanistan Bangladesh Bhutan the Islamic Republic of Iran Maldives Nepal Pakistan and Sri Lanka. In addition three thematic studies were commissioned on India government regulation and accountability lowfee private schools and publicprivate partnerships in technical and vocational education and training one on Pakistan ancillary services and one on the South Asia region teacher education.The Regional Report includes uptodate information referencing COVID19 noting that the regions private providers were particularly hit by the pandemic. The editorial board which consists of six prominent partners from five countries Institute for Integrated Development Studies Nepal Central Square Foundation India Centre for Policy Research India Institute for Policy Studies Sri Lanka ITA Pakistan and BRAC Bangladesh met in April for the first time. The strategic objectives are to advance national and regional dialogue. Launch events are scheduled to take place in November in India Nepal and Pakistan as well as a fullday event at the South Asia Association for Regional Cooperation.
